option_a: Be able to fly, but only at walking speed
option_b: Run at 100mph, but never fly
hook: No right answer — just pick one!
debate_note: Flight = freedom. Speed = pure utility. Which matters more?

option_a: Know every language in the world
option_b: Play every musical instrument perfectly
hook: You can only choose one for life
debate_note: Communication vs. art. Which opens more doors?

option_a: Always be 10 minutes early
option_b: Always be 10 minutes late
hook: You have NO choice — it's permanent
debate_note: Early = reliable but stressed. Late = relaxed but judged.

option_a: Only be able to eat sweet foods forever
option_b: Only be able to eat savoury foods forever
hook: Choose wisely — this is for life
debate_note: No chocolate, cake, or ice cream vs. no pizza, pasta, or steak.

option_a: Be invisible whenever you want
option_b: Read minds whenever you want
debate_note: Invisibility = freedom. Mind reading = truth. But can you handle the truth?

option_a: Have unlimited money but live alone forever
option_b: Be surrounded by loved ones but always broke
hook: This one will tell you a lot about yourself
debate_note: Money vs. connection — the oldest question.

option_a: Speak every language but only speak in rhymes
option_b: Know one language but speak normally
hook: One is useful, one is chaos
debate_note: Imagine job interviews. Imagine arguments. In rhyme.

option_a: Live 200 years but look 90 the whole time
option_b: Live 70 years but look 25 the whole time
debate_note: Would you trade your looks for double the life?

option_a: Have superhuman strength
option_b: Have superhuman speed
debate_note: Strength = power. Speed = escape, arrive anywhere, save anyone faster.

option_a: Know the exact date of your death
option_b: Not know, but live 20 years longer
debate_note: The certainty might let you plan — or it might haunt every day.

option_a: Eat your favourite meal every day but nothing else
option_b: Never eat your favourite meal again
debate_note: Repetition kills enjoyment. But giving it up forever?

option_a: Be the smartest person in any room
option_b: Be the funniest person in any room
debate_note: Smart people solve problems. Funny people survive them.

option_a: Always feel too hot
option_b: Always feel too cold
debate_note: Cold = add layers. Heat = can't remove your skin.

option_a: Travel the world broke for 1 year
option_b: Stay home with $100k you can't spend on travel
debate_note: Memories you can't buy vs. security you can actually use.

option_a: Never need sleep ever again
option_b: Get paid $500 every time you sleep 8 hours
debate_note: No sleep = 8 extra hours daily. $500/sleep = $182k/year for doing nothing.

option_a: Have a photographic memory
option_b: Forget all your bad memories
debate_note: Perfect recall includes every embarrassment. Clean slate erases trauma.

option_a: Be able to pause time
option_b: Be able to rewind time by 10 minutes
debate_note: Pause = unlimited time. Rewind = undo mistakes. Which would you use more?

option_a: Hiccup once a minute for the rest of your life
option_b: Sneeze 10 times every hour for the rest of your life
hook: Both are terrible — pick your suffering
debate_note: Sneezing is exhausting. Hiccups are distracting. Vote in the comments.

option_a: Be able to control fire
option_b: Be able to control water
debate_note: Fire = offense and warmth. Water = covers 71% of Earth and most of your body.

option_a: Only eat at McDonald's for a year
option_b: Never eat fast food again
hook: A year of golden arches OR never again?
debate_note: You CAN eat salads at McDonald's. But forever without? No pizza? No chips?

option_a: Have an extra $10,000 right now
option_b: Have your biggest insecurity permanently erased
debate_note: Some insecurities cost far more than $10k in therapy.

option_a: Be extremely attractive but dumb
option_b: Be extremely smart but unattractive
debate_note: Attractiveness opens doors. Intelligence keeps them open.

option_a: Fight 100 duck-sized horses
option_b: Fight 1 horse-sized duck
debate_note: 100 tiny hooves vs. one MASSIVE beak. The numbers vs. the trauma.

option_a: Be famous but hated
option_b: Be unknown but universally loved by everyone you meet
debate_note: Fame is loud. Being loved by everyone who knows you is quiet — and rarer.

option_a: Teleport anywhere instantly
option_b: Time travel but only to the past (no changes allowed)
debate_note: Teleportation changes your daily life completely. Time travel is just tourism with guilt.

option_a: Never have to work again but be permanently bored
option_b: Love your job but work 80 hours a week
debate_note: No work sounds great until you have nothing to do. 80 hours sounds brutal until you love it.

option_a: Always say exactly what you think
option_b: Never be able to tell the truth
debate_note: Total honesty destroys relationships. Total lying makes them hollow.

option_a: Win $1 million but can never tell anyone how you got it
option_b: Win $100k that everyone knows about
hook: Wealth with a secret or modest fame?
debate_note: A secret million is powerful. Public $100k invites requests from everyone you know.

option_a: Have the ability to breathe underwater
option_b: Have the ability to survive in space without a suit
hook: Explore the ocean or the stars?
debate_note: 70% of Earth is ocean, 99% unexplored. Space is infinite but far.

option_a: Never feel physical pain
option_b: Never feel emotional pain
debate_note: No physical pain sounds great until you can't tell you're injured. Emotional pain signals danger too.

option_a: Eat a tablespoon of wasabi
option_b: Eat a tablespoon of Vegemite
hook: One is agony, one is an acquired taste
debate_note: Wasabi burns for 2 minutes max. Vegemite is forever traumatic if you're not Australian.

option_a: Talk to animals
option_b: Talk to plants
hook: Which conversations would actually be useful?
debate_note: Animals warn you about danger. Plants… take a very long time to get to the point.

option_a: Be the best at everything you try but only for one hour
option_b: Be decent at everything forever
debate_note: One hour of genius per skill is powerful. Permanent mediocrity is safe.

option_a: Every song you've ever liked suddenly sounds terrible to you
option_b: Every movie you've ever loved becomes unwatchable
debate_note: Music is everywhere — loss is constant. Movies you can avoid. Which do you use more?

option_a: Be 10 years older than you are now
option_b: Be 10 years younger with no memories of those years
hook: Time is not on your side either way
debate_note: Older = more wisdom, less time. Younger = more time, less experience.

option_a: Gain 20kg overnight
option_b: Lose all your hair overnight
hook: Both happen tonight. Pick the lesser evil.
debate_note: Weight can be worked off. Hair might not come back.

option_a: Have legs for arms and arms for legs
option_b: Have your head where your stomach is and your stomach where your head is
debate_note: Both are horrifying. The question is which is more functional.

option_a: Find your true love but they live on the other side of the world
option_b: Never find true love but have an amazing friend group
debate_note: Long distance is hard. But loneliness without close friends is harder.

option_a: Have free WiFi everywhere you go for life
option_b: Have free food everywhere you go for life
debate_note: Free food = survival. Free WiFi = productivity, entertainment, connection. Which runs out first?

option_a: Always win every argument
option_b: Always know when you're wrong
debate_note: Winning arguments feels good but isolates. Knowing when you're wrong is genuinely rare and powerful.

option_a: Have your phone battery always at 100%
option_b: Never feel hungry or thirsty again
debate_note: No hunger = massive time and money saved. Full battery = never anxious about your phone dying.

option_a: Live in your favourite city but be broke
option_b: Live somewhere boring but be comfortable financially
debate_note: A great city costs money to enjoy anyway. Comfort anywhere buys experiences.

option_a: Be able to stop time
option_b: Be immortal (but aging normally)
debate_note: Stopping time gives unlimited productivity. Immortality is just eternal aging.

option_a: Skip traffic forever
option_b: Never be cold again
debate_note: Traffic wastes years of your life. But cold is constant misery.

option_a: Go back to high school knowing everything you know now
option_b: Fast-forward 10 years with $1 million in your account
debate_note: Past = chance to reshape your life. Future = skip the struggle.

option_a: Be able to speak to the dead for 5 minutes
option_b: Know your future for the next 10 years
hook: One conversation with the past or a map of the future?
debate_note: 5 minutes with anyone who's gone. Or certainty about what's coming.

option_a: Always sneeze when someone says your name
option_b: Always laugh when someone cries
hook: Both will ruin your social life
debate_note: Sneezing is annoying but harmless. Laughing at grief is a social catastrophe.

option_a: Know the Wi-Fi password of every place you enter
option_b: Never wait in a queue longer than 1 minute
debate_note: Free WiFi anywhere = hundreds of dollars saved. Zero queuing = years of your life returned.

option_a: Be able to talk to your pet
option_b: Have your pet live as long as you do
debate_note: Conversation reveals if they're happy. But would you want to know what they really think?

option_a: Have no one show up to your wedding
option_b: Have no one show up to your funeral
debate_note: No wedding guests = humiliation while alive. No funeral guests = you'll never know — but still.

option_a: Only be able to whisper for the rest of your life
option_b: Only be able to shout for the rest of your life
hook: Volume is now out of your hands
debate_note: Whispering in loud places = isolation. Shouting in quiet places = constant embarrassment.

option_a: Have the superpower to heal others but not yourself
option_b: Heal yourself instantly but never be able to help others
debate_note: Healing others is heroic but painful. Healing yourself is practical but isolating.

option_a: Be able to read 10 times faster
option_b: Remember everything you've ever read
debate_note: Speed = more input. Memory = better output. Which changes your life more?

option_a: Never have to exercise but stay perfectly healthy
option_b: Never have to sleep but feel fully rested
hook: Which chore would you drop forever?
debate_note: No exercise = ~5 hours/week back. No sleep = ~56 hours/week back.

option_a: Have the ability to delete any memory
option_b: Be able to replay any memory in perfect detail
hook: Memory is power — how do you use it?
debate_note: Deletion = remove regret. Replay = relive every perfect moment.

option_a: Always know when someone is lying to you
option_b: Always be believed when you tell the truth
hook: Detect lies or be trusted completely?
debate_note: Knowing lies is exhausting but protective. Being believed = infinite credibility.

option_a: Give up social media forever
option_b: Give up watching TV and movies forever
hook: Which one can you actually live without?
debate_note: No social media = less FOMO, more time. No movies/TV = less entertainment, more production?

option_a: Be able to survive without food
option_b: Be able to survive without water
hook: Which biological need would you drop?
debate_note: Food = time, money, and logistics. Water = you'd be unstoppable in a crisis.

option_a: Be completely fluent in every coding language
option_b: Be able to master any physical skill in 24 hours
debate_note: Code fluency = massive career power. Physical skill mastery = you can do literally anything.

option_a: Have $1 million but must spend it all in 24 hours
option_b: Get $1,000 per day for the rest of your life
debate_note: $1M in 24h = ~$41k/hour, mostly wasted. $1k/day = $365k/year forever. Maths wins.
